title: A rhombus-shaped tetranuclear dysprosium cluster showing single-molecule magnet behavior

synthesis.procedure: A solution of Dy(tmhd)3·2H2O (0.025 mmol) in 18.0 mL of CH3CN was heated to 70 °C for 30 min. Then a CH2Cl2 solution (3.0 mL) containing HL (0.025 mmol) was added. The mixture was stirred for another 4 h at 70 °C and then cooled to room temperature. After filtration, the resulting solution was kept in the dark and concentrated slowly by evaporation at 4 °C. After about 4 days, block-shaped yellow crystals were obtained.
synthesis.time: 30 min heating; additional 4 h stirring; about 4 days crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by filtration and slow evaporation in the dark
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtration; concentrate slowly by evaporation at 4 °C in the dark; block-shaped yellow crystals after about 4 days.

properties.summary: Rhombus-shaped Dy4 cluster 1 shows SMM behavior with slow magnetic relaxation under zero dc field. Room-temperature χMT is 56.32 cm3 K mol−1 versus 56.68 cm3 K mol−1 expected for four isolated Dy(III) ions, falling to 40.11 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, attributed to thermal depopulation of Stark sublevels and/or weak antiferromagnetic Dy···Dy interactions. Frequency-dependent in-phase and out-of-phase ac signals (3.0 Oe ac, zero dc) with χ″ peaks at 6.0–10.0 K indicate slow magnetization relaxation; a low-T upturn below 5 K without peaks to 2 K is ascribed to QTM. Arrhenius fit above 8.0 K (8.0–12.0 K) gives ΔE/kB = 69.29 K and τ0 = 6.18×10−8 s. A Raman/Orbach/direct model over 2.0–12.0 K gives n = 5.27, A = 0.4578 s−1 K−5.27, C = 0.0778. Cole–Cole α = 0.38–0.59 (4.0–12.0 K) indicates a broad distribution of relaxation times and possible multiple processes below ~5 K.
